speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you have a rash along with fever, runny nose, and headache. To help narrow this down, can you tell me when your symptoms first started and if anyone around you has been sick recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: That facial rash sparing the mouth is a very specific clue. Did you or anyone else at home have a similar rash or a recent sore throat around that same time? Also, have you noticed any redness on your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP). Additionally, can you confirm if the rash on your hands and feet is also sparing the fingertips and toes?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC Normal, Hemoglobin Normal, Platelets Slightly elevated; C-Reactive Protein: Not provided in data. Rash on hands and feet: Not observed (patient presentation indicates rash on trunk and extremities with facial involvement sparing the perioral area).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (likely Group A Streptococcus pharyngitis with a rash, though the "sandpaper" quality is not explicitly described, the combination of fever, headache, and rash is highly suggestive; however, given the specific mention of facial rash sparing the perioral area, I am reconsidering towards Measles or a viral exanthem, but the lack of hand/foot rash makes Scarlet Fever less likely.
